card.description:
### **Description**

**Schedule**: Exempt, min 40 Hours per week | Monday - Friday | 8am - 4:30pm 
**Department:** Interdisciplinary | Muskegon, Mi
 
 
**What You’ll Do:**

Lead a dedicated interdisciplinary team in delivering high-quality, participant-centered care through the PACE model. You'll coach and mentor team members, collaborate with organizational leaders, and empower participants to achieve their goals while promoting independence, dignity, and overall well-being.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Lead, mentor, and support a high-performing interdisciplinary team.
* Facilitate IDT meetings and promote collaboration, accountability, and participant-centered decision-making.
* Support onboarding, training, and ongoing team development.
* Monitor team and participant outcomes using data to drive continuous improvement.
* Foster exceptional customer service and a culture aligned with LifeCircles' mission, vision, and values.

**Care Planning & Coordination**

* Guide comprehensive care planning that reflects participant goals, preferences, and needs.
* Partner with interdisciplinary teams, departments, and external providers to ensure coordinated care.
* Oversee implementation of care plans and service delivery.
* Support participant eligibility, enrollment, and care transitions through strong understanding of PACE requirements.
* Identify and address high-risk clinical, behavioral, or operational concerns.

**Operations & Quality**

* Ensure compliance with PACE regulations, organizational standards, and quality initiatives.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including participant outcomes and service utilization.
* Support effective use of the electronic medical record (EMR) and operational processes.
* Lead quality improvement efforts that enhance care delivery, efficiency, and participant experience.
* Participate in audits, surveys, and regulatory reviews.
* *Additional duties may be assigned as needed.*

*The above is a summary of the position, it in no way states or implies that these are the only duties this position will be required to perform. If selected for the position you will receive a full job description.*

 

### **Skills, Knowledge and Expertise**

 

* Bachelor's degree in a healthcare-related field required; Master's degree preferred.
* Professional licensure (RN, LMSW/LLMSW, RD, PT, OT, or similar) preferred.
* Current CPR certification or willingness to obtain.
* Valid Michigan driver's license and reliable transportation required.

* Minimum of one (1) year of experience working with frail older adults required; three (3) or more years of experience in an interdisciplinary, team-based healthcare setting preferred.
* Leadership or supervisory experience in PACE, managed care, home health, hospice, geriatrics, or a related healthcare environment preferred.
* Experience leading interdisciplinary teams and coordinating participant-centered care.
* Experience with care coordination, service utilization, population health, or quality improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated ability to support operational excellence, process improvement, and change management efforts.

* Knowledge of PACE regulations, CMS requirements, and Medicaid guidelines.
* Strong leadership, coaching, team-building, and relationship-management skills.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and drive operational excellence.
* Experience using data and performance metrics to support decision-making.
* Strong critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and electronic health record (EHR) systems.
* Ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines and influence positive outcomes.

 

### **Benefits**

 

* **Generous 6 weeks of Flexible time off per year**—plus **paid holidays** on top of that.
* **Competitive Benefits for Full-Time Team Members** – Enjoy Medical, Vision & Dental Insurance starting on the 1st of the month after 30 days of hire.
* **Retirement Savings Plan** – Secure your future with employer contributions.
* **Daily Pay** –Instantly transfer your daily earnings.
* **Team Member Referral Bonus Program** – Earn $500 when you bring great people to our team!
* **Career Growth & Development** – Advance your career with tuition assistance and school scholarships up to $3,000 per semester.
* **Wellness Program & Reimbursemen**t – Prioritize your health and well-being, reimbursed 120 a year!
* **Mileage Reimbursement** – Offered for work-related travel.

### **About Brio Living Services**

Brio Living Services is dedicated to enriching the lives of seniors through exceptional, faith-based, nonprofit senior living communities. Offering a full continuum of care, including independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, and memory care, Brio provides maintenance-free lifestyles and personalized support to meet residents' evolving needs. With a focus on wellness, connection, and vibrant aging, Brio empowers residents to pursue their interests, build meaningful relationships, and thrive in welcoming communities.

Brio Living Services does not use artificial intelligence (AI) to make employment decisions. All applications and resumes are reviewed by members of our hiring team, and human oversight remains an essential part of the recruitment process. AI may be used only to assist with administrative tasks, such as organizing information, summarizing reviewed materials, and collecting notes.

Brio Living Services is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation during the application process, please contact us at **loveyourcareer@mybrio.org**. Language assistance may also be available for applicants who require support in a language other than English. Please reach out so we can discuss your needs and available resources.

Brio Living Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer and provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other protected status under applicable federal, state, or local laws.

card.description:
The University of Nevada, Reno (UNR) appreciates your interest in employment at our growing institution. We want your application process to go smoothly and quickly. Final applications must be submitted prior to the close of the recruitment.

 

If you need assistance or have questions regarding the application process, please contact our recruitment helpline at (775) 784-1495 or jobs@unr.edu .

**Job Description**

The Orvis School of Nursing at the University of Nevada, Reno is recruiting for a Director of Faculty Practice Operations within the Office of Strategic Partnerships and Practice (OSPP). The Director of Faculty Practice Operations provides senior-level operational, managerial, and partnership execution leadership for the Office of Strategic Partnerships and Practice (OSPP). This role is responsible for the day-to-day operations and growth of all OSPP practice sites and initiatives, ensuring efficient, compliant, and sustainable operations in alignment with strategic priorities established by the Associate Dean for Strategic Partnerships and Practice (ADSPP). The Director brings strong business and financial acumen, practice management experience, grants and contracts experience, and expertise in community-based partnerships. This position will possess a working knowledge of healthcare reimbursement, medical billing and coding, revenue cycle management, and payer contracting processes in insurance-reimbursed clinical environments. The Director operationalizes strategy through strong infrastructure, systems, partnerships, and team leadership and assumes operational accountability for the financial, compliance, and reputational risk associated with OSPP practice sites, partnerships, and funded initiatives.

 

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree and four (4) years of related professional work experience; **OR**

Master’s degree and two (2) years of related professional work experience.

**Related Experience** : Progressively responsible experience in practice management, operations, partnerships, or related leadership roles; experience in healthcare reimbursement, medical billing, coding, and revenue cycle processes, including the ability to work effectively with payer contracts, compliance requirements, and practice finance operations; experience working in a practice environment with evolving priorities and operational needs; people management and team leadership experience or a related field.

 

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration (MBA) or Master of Healthcare Administration (MHA)
* Eligible for RN licensure in Nevada
* Experience in academic health sciences, higher education, or community-based organizations
* Experience supporting faculty practice, community-engaged scholarship, or interprofessional initiatives
A demonstrated commitment to equity, community engagement, and collaboration 

 

**Schedule and Travel Requirements**

* Variable work schedule
Occasional travel may be required 

**Compensation Grade**

Administrative Faculty – C

To view the salary schedule for this position, please visit: Salary Schedules and select Administrative Faculty by Grade. Salary is competitive and commensurate with related education and experience.

**Remarkable Retirement**

Our retirement plan is beyond compare. Your 19.25% contribution is generously matched by the University. With the faculty retirement plan, you are 100% vested your first day. Sit back and watch your retirement dollars grow! All permanent employees on an annual "A" or "B" contract who are employed at least 50% full-time are eligible to participate in the NSHE retirement program unless they are members of PERS of Nevada.

**Perks of Working at UNR**

* Health insurance options including dental and vision - Health Insurance
* Generous annual, sick leave, long term disability and life insurance – Faculty Benefits
* E. L. Wiegand Fitness Center offers annual or semester memberships and spouse/domestic partner membership options. E.L. Wiegand Fitness Center

* Reno is proud to be a University town! Many local businesses offer discounts to WolfCard holders
* Mountain EAP supports employees (and eligible dependents) through life's difficult moments. Mountain EAP is located in Reno and specializes in counseling and advising services for personal or interpersonal issues.
* Faculty Senate is the principal representing body for faculty. Its membership includes representatives from each academic and administrative major unit of the University. Faculty Senate
No state income tax! 

 

**Grants-in-Aid for Faculty Employees**

The University is proud to provide a reduced-rate tuition benefit to faculty and qualified dependents. Faculty can take up to six credits per semester at a reduced rate. Dependents of faculty have unlimited credits, but in order to be eligible children must be unmarried and under the age of 24 and must receive at least 50% of their financial support from the employee and/or employee’s spouse or domestic partner. Faculty Grants-in-Aid

 

**Faculty Dual Career Assistance Program**

The University of Nevada, Reno recognizes the importance of addressing dual-career couples’ professional needs. We offer a dual career assistance program to newly hired faculty spouses/partners that provides resources and assists them to identify career opportunities in Northern Nevada. Dual Career Assistance Program

 

**Department Information**

https://www.unr.edu/nursing

**Exempt**

Yes

**Full-Time Equivalent**

100.0%

**Required Attachment(s)**

Please note, once you submit your application the only attachment/s viewable to you will be the attachment/s to the resume/CV section of the application. Any additional required attachment/s to the cover letter, references, additional documents sections of the application, will not be viewable to you after you submit your application. All uploaded attachment/s will be on the application for the committee to review. To request updates to attachments, prior to the committee review of applications, please contact the candidate helpdesk at jobs@unr.edu .

**Please attach the following documents to your application**

1) Resume/CV

2) Cover Letter

3) Contact Information for three professional references

**This posting is open until filled**

Qualified individuals are encouraged to apply immediately. This search will close without notice when a sufficient number of applications are received, or a hiring decision has been made.

**Posting Close Date**

Note to Applicant

A background check will be conducted on the candidate(s) selected for hire.

HR will attempt to verify academic credentials upon receipt of hiring documents. If the academic credentials cannot be verified, HR will notify the faculty member that an official transcript of their highest degree must be submitted within thirty days of the faculty member’s first day of employment.

References will be contacted at the appropriate phase of the recruitment process.

Applicants hired on a federal contract may be subject to E-Verify.

As part of the hiring process, applicants for positions in the Nevada System of Higher Education may be required to demonstrate the ability to perform job-related tasks.

For positions that require driving, evidence of a valid driver's license will be required at the time of employment and as a condition of continued employment.

Schedules are subject to change based on organizational needs.

The University of Nevada, Reno is committed to providing a place of work and learning free of discrimination on the basis of a person’s age (40 or older), disability, whether actual or perceived by others (including service-connected disabilities), gender (including pregnancy related conditions), military status or military obligations, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, national origin, race (including hair texture and protected hairstyles such as natural hairstyles, afros, bantu knots, curls, braids, locks and twists), color, or religion (protected classes).

**About Us**

The University of Nevada, Reno is a leading public research university committed to the promise of a future powered by knowledge. Founded in 1874 as Nevada’s original land-grant university, the University serves more than 23,000 undergraduate and graduate students from all 50 states and 63 countries.

Classified by the Carnegie® Classification of Institutions of Higher Education as an R1 (“Very High Research”) university, it is also recognized in the Carnegie® Community Engagement classification. The University is also ranked by U.S. News & World Report among the “Best National Universities” and “Best National Public Universities.” It also ranks in the top tier of the WSJ/Times Higher Education World University Rankings and the New York Times’ “Top Colleges for Economic Diversity.”

Since 2009, nearly $1 billion has been has invested in advanced labs, facilities, and residence halls on the main campus. The University is home to Nevada’s first medical school – the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine and the Wayne L. Prim Campus at Lake Tahoe, where education, research, and creative work thrive in a stunning mountain setting. The University delivers on its original land-grant mission with outreach across the state through the University of Nevada, Reno Extension, Nevada Agricultural Experiment Station, Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology, Nevada Small Business Development Center, the Nevada Seismological Laboratory, and Wolf Pack Athletics.

The main campus is in Reno, Nevada, a burgeoning global technology hub with a vibrant midtown and downtown. Found where the high desert of the Great Basin meets the High Sierra and Lake Tahoe, the beautiful, 290-acre main campus is also a Nevada State Arboretum. The University’s physical infrastructure is expanding with ongoing construction of the newly named John Tullock Business Building, set to open in fall 2025. Groundbreaking is also planned for a new State Public Health Laboratory Building on campus, alongside the recent acquisition of 16 parcels near campus, known as “University Village,” to provide affordable housing for graduate students and early career faculty.

Collaborating with world-renowned organizations, the University fosters innovation through initiatives such as the Digital Wolf Pack partnership with Apple, which ensures equitable access to technology for students, providing new incoming freshman or transfer students with an iPad Air and accessories. Google’s TechWise initiate is an 18-month program that fully supports undergraduate students in becoming entry-level software engineers by graduation.

In 2023, the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Economic Development Administration (EDA) announced that Nevada – led by the University of Nevada, Reno – was named one of the inaugural 31 Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs (TechHubs). Nevada was selected from a competitive pool of 489 applicants from across the United States and its territories. Nevada’s Tech Hub will strengthen America’s lithium batteries, critical elements and other electric vehicle materials industry sectors within the state.

Through its commitment to high-impact education, world-improving research and creative activity, and outreach that’s transforming Nevada’s communities and businesses, the University continues its 150-year tradition of benefitting our state, nation and world.

The University recognizes that diversity promotes excellence in education and research. The inclusive and engaged community on campus recognizes the added value that students, faculty, and staff from different backgrounds bring to the educational experience.

Today, the University delivers on its original land-grant mission of access to education and knowledge by investing in the academics, facilities, support, engagement and vibrant campus life that promote our diverse students’ cognitive growth and academic achievement – all while remaining one of the best values in American higher education.

For more information, please visit the University’s website .

card.description:
Director of Operations – Dave’s Hot Chicken

**Position:** Director of Operations

**Employment Type:** Full-Time

**Industry:** Restaurant / Multi-Unit Operations

About the Role

Dave’s Hot Chicken is looking for a highly motivated, results-driven **Director of Operations** to lead and support our growing restaurant operations.

This position is responsible for driving operational excellence across multiple locations while developing strong leaders, building a high-performance culture, delivering an exceptional guest experience, and achieving financial results.

We are looking for a leader who understands that great restaurant operations start with **great people**. The Director of Operations will work closely with General Managers and restaurant leadership teams to create accountability, consistency, and a culture where team members feel supported, challenged, recognized, and given opportunities to grow.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Leadership

* Provide leadership and oversight for multiple Dave’s Hot Chicken locations.
* Ensure restaurants consistently execute Dave’s Hot Chicken operational standards, food quality, cleanliness, hospitality, and brand expectations.
* Conduct regular restaurant visits and provide clear, actionable feedback to leadership teams.
* Identify operational opportunities and develop plans to improve restaurant performance.
* Ensure restaurants are properly staffed and prepared to execute at a high level.
* Maintain strong standards for food safety, workplace safety, and regulatory compliance.

People & Leadership Development

* Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing General Managers and restaurant leaders.
* Build a strong pipeline of future General Managers, Area Leaders, and other operations leaders.
* Create individualized development plans for key leaders and high-potential team members.
* Hold leaders accountable while providing the coaching, tools, and resources necessary for them to succeed.
* Recognize outstanding performance and create a culture where accomplishments are celebrated.
* Ensure leaders are actively developing their teams rather than simply managing daily operations.
* Promote a culture of respect, communication, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

Financial Performance

* Take ownership of restaurant sales, profitability, labor, food cost, controllable expenses, and overall financial performance.
* Analyze P&L statements and restaurant performance reports to identify trends and opportunities.
* Develop action plans to improve underperforming locations.
* Partner with restaurant leadership to increase sales while maintaining appropriate labor and cost controls.
* Establish clear performance expectations and follow up consistently on results.

Guest Experience

* Ensure every restaurant delivers a consistently outstanding guest experience.
* Monitor guest feedback and identify recurring opportunities.
* Coach restaurant leaders on hospitality, speed of service, order accuracy, food quality, and restaurant cleanliness.
* Ensure guest concerns are handled quickly, professionally, and appropriately.

New Restaurant Openings & Growth

* Support new restaurant openings, including staffing, training, leadership development, and operational readiness.
* Build leadership benches ahead of organizational growth.
* Help establish scalable systems and processes as the organization adds locations.
* Partner with senior leadership to develop strategies that support long-term growth.

What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate will have:

* 7+ years of progressive restaurant operations leadership experience.
* 3+ years of successful multi-unit leadership experience.
* Experience overseeing multiple high-volume restaurant locations.
* Proven ability to develop General Managers and build leadership pipelines.
* Strong understanding of restaurant P&L management, labor, food cost, sales building, and profitability.
* Demonstrated ability to improve restaurant performance and hold teams accountable for results.
* Experience supporting new restaurant openings is strongly preferred.
* Excellent communication, coaching, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to balance **people, operations, guest experience, and profitability**.
* Willingness to travel regularly between restaurant locations.
* Must be willing to work weekend, nights and availability to travel.

The Leader We Want

We are looking for someone who:

* **Leads from the front** and is comfortable spending significant time inside the restaurants.
* Builds relationships and earns the trust of their teams.
* Sets high expectations without losing sight of the people responsible for delivering the results.
* Develops leaders instead of simply giving directions.
* Recognizes and rewards great performance.
* Communicates clearly and follows through on commitments.
* Makes decisions based on both operational data and what is actually happening inside the restaurants.
* Takes ownership and expects the same from their leadership team.
* Understands that sustainable financial performance comes from strong operations, strong leadership, and engaged teams.
* Is passionate about building a winning culture while growing the Dave’s Hot Chicken brand.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this position means:

**Great People. Great Restaurants. Great Guest Experiences. Strong Financial Results.**

The Director of Operations will be expected to build restaurants where team members want to work, leaders have opportunities to grow, guests want to return, and the business consistently delivers strong results.

Why Join Dave’s Hot Chicken?

This is an opportunity to play a significant leadership role in a rapidly growing restaurant brand. You will have the ability to influence operations, develop future leaders, support restaurant growth, and help create a culture built around accountability, recognition, development, and operational excellence.

**Dave’s Hot Chicken is an Equal Opportunity Employer.** We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

card.description:
**Position Summary** 
**RadioMedix is seeking a proven leader to serve as Director of Preclinical Operations, heading our R&D and preclinical team and running our in vitro biology and in vivo imaging and vivarium laboratories, in close partnership with our radiochemistry team. This person will t****ake** **radioligand therapy (RLT) and diagnostic candidates** **from discovery and lead optimization through candidate selection and** **IND-****enabling studie****s, on time and with data that stands up to regulatory review. We are looking for a forward-thinking builder with a track record of leading high-performing teams, who will** **oversee a Lab Manager responsible for day****-****to-day lab** **operations, modernize our labs with new software and systems, and set the standard for a clean, safe, well-run research environment.** 
 
**About RadioMedix** 
**RadioMedix is a Houston-based, clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company developing targeted diagnostics and radioligand therapeutics for cancer and other serious diseases. Our work spans discovery, preclinical development, clinical studies, and manufacturing, with programs built on isotopes such as Pb-212, Ga-68, and Cu-64.** 
**Key responsibilities:**
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* **Team leadership:**
 + Provide strategic and operational leadership across Biology and Pharmacology, overseeing both in vitro and in vivo research teams.
 + Lead, hire, develop, and expand multidisciplinary R&D and preclinical scientific teams in support of the company's growing research organization, setting clear goals, priorities, and accountability.
 + Foster a high-performing, collaborative research organization with a culture of scientific rigor, radiation safety, and ownership.
 + Mentor scientific leaders, coach managers and scientists, run performance reviews, and plan succession and career growth.
 + Balance workload across concurrent programs and make resourcing calls when priorities shift.
* **Laboratory operations:**
 + Manage and oversee the Lab Manager, who runs day-to-day operation of the cell biology and in vivo (vivarium) laboratories; set priorities, performance goals, and operating metrics, and review lab performance regularly.
 + Own lab budgets and capital purchases, and oversee the Lab Manager's management of equipment (dose calibrators, gamma counters, and preclinical SPECT/PET/CT imaging systems), maintenance and calibration, and supply inventory.
 + Plan and secure isotope supply for research, coordinating delivery schedules with study timelines.
 + Maintain compliance with the radioactive materials license, ALARA principles, and dosimetry and waste-handling programs, in partnership with the Radiation Safety Officer (RSO).
 + Oversee animal research compliance with IACUC protocols and AAALAC or OLAW standards, where applicable.
 + Ensure biosafety, chemical hygiene, and radioactive material receipt and shipping (DOT/IATA) programs are in place and followed.
 + Implement SOPs, data integrity practices, electronic lab notebooks, and inspection-ready documentation.
* **Lab standards and housekeeping:**
 + Set and enforce clear standards for lab cleanliness, organization, and housekeeping across all preclinical labs and vivarium areas.
 + Hold the Lab Manager accountable for assigning owners to each lab area, with routine walk-throughs, cleaning and contamination-survey schedules, and accountability for findings.
 + Keep labs inspection-ready at all times for radiation safety, IACUC, and partner or client audits.
* **R&D and preclinical** **program execution:**
 + Establish and execute biology and pharmacology strategies across target validation, drug discovery, and preclinical development.
 + Oversee in vitro and in vivo studies, including assay development, disease models, mechanism of action, and preclinical efficacy.
 + Drive the advancement of therapeutic programs from target validation through candidate selection and IND submission.
 + Evaluate research data, guide program strategy, and make recommendations on scientific direction and prioritization.
 + Establish research capabilities, processes, and infrastructure to support the company's expanding pipeline.
 + Run a stage-gate process with clear candidate selection criteria (binding affinity, tumor uptake and retention, normal-organ clearance, in vivo stability, and therapeutic index) and regular portfolio reviews with leadership.
 + Design and deliver preclinical packages for radioligand therapeutics and companion diagnostics: binding affinity, internalization, and efflux assays, serum and in vivo stability, biodistribution and pharmacokinetics in tumor-bearing models, SPECT/CT and PET/CT imaging, efficacy and maximum tolerated dose studies, dosimetry with extrapolation to human, and IND-enabling toxicology.
 + Translate program goals into study plans with milestones, budgets, and go/no-go criteria.
 + Integrate DMPK, toxicology, translational sciences, and other research functions to advance pipeline programs, aligning study designs, timelines, and data across disciplines.
 + Oversee DMPK and radiopharmacokinetic characterization, including biodistribution, clearance and excretion, metabolism, and in vivo stability, to inform candidate selection, dosing, and dosimetry.
 + Direct the design and oversight of IND-enabling toxicology studies, in-house or at CROs, including dose selection, assessment of radiation-related and off-target toxicities, and integration with dosimetry.
 + Lead translational science activities, including biomarker and patient-selection strategies, imaging-based target engagement, and extrapolation to a safe first-in-human dose, in partnership with clinical development.
 + Select and manage CROs and academic collaborators, including toxicology studies, scopes of work, budgets, and data quality.
 + Author and review preclinical sections of IND, IMPD, and other regulatory submissions, and support responses to FDA and other agencies.
 + Track program timelines and report progress, risks, and recommendations to leadership.
 + Partner with the radiochemistry team on radiolabeled compound supply, quality specifications, and study scheduling, and provide preclinical data that informs radiochemistry and CMC decisions.
 + Ensure studies are well designed and statistically sound and produce complete, traceable data packages and study reports suitable for regulatory submissions and publication.
* **Cross-functional and business support:**
 + Work closely with radiochemistry, CMC, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, and clinical teams to move candidates smoothly from bench to first-in-human studies.
 + Support business development and partnership activity, including technical due diligence, partner presentations, and preclinical work for collaborators and CDMO clients.
 + Contribute to grant applications, publications, and scientific conference presentations.
 + Evaluate new targets and isotopes, and partner with radiochemistry on chelator and linker selection, to strengthen the pipeline.
 + Capture inventions through invention disclosures and support patent counsel on filings that protect the pipeline.

**Qualifications**

* **Education:** PhD in Pharmacology, Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, or a related discipline strongly preferred. Exceptional candidates with a Master's degree will also be considered.

* **Experience:**
 + 10+ years of biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry experience in drug discovery, biology, and/or pharmacology, including 5+ years in radiopharmaceuticals.
 + Proven track record of advancing therapeutic programs, ideally radioligand therapeutics (RLTs) or theranostic agents, through IND submission, with direct involvement in multiple INDs.

A family-like atmosphere known for growth opportunities and a low turnover rate in the industry.

AWG is expanding and seeking exceptional talent to drive our progress forward. Don't miss out on a promising future — join our team today!

Our company provides industrial, medical, and specialty gases as well as food and beverage gases across the United States, from Montana to Pennsylvania and down through Texas and Florida. card.description:
Description:

The Director of Operations leads assigned day-to-day operational functions across Heartview locations and is responsible for consistent, efficient, safe, and accountable operations. The position partners with organizational leaders to strengthen operating systems, management reporting, staffing efficiency, patient access, and resource utilization while respecting established clinical and medical authority.

**What You'll Do:**

* Lead and supervise the Bismarck, Cando, and Dickinson Site Directors, Director of Admissions, and Maintenance leadership.
* Provide leadership, guidance, and professional development to assigned managers and department leaders; establish clear performance expectations and accountability for results.
* Monitor staffing utilization, service capacity, workflows, patient-support functions, and operational performance across assigned locations.
* Partner with Heartview leaders to establish useful operating measures, reporting routines, key performance indicators, and practical accountability systems.
* Work with administrative and clinical leaders to improve patient flow and utilization of available services while respecting clinical and medical needs.
* Oversee maintenance, grounds, janitorial services, fleet operations, and preventive maintenance priorities.
* Identify operational gaps across residential, outpatient, and medication-assisted treatment services; collaborate with appropriate leadership to develop and implement solutions.
* Travel required 2 - 4 days per month.

**Why Work With Us?** At Heartview Foundation, we take pride in supporting not only our patients but also our team. We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:

* Generous **Paid Time Off (PTO)** for work-life balance.
* **401(k) with employer match** to support your financial goals.
* **100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision** insurance coverage for **employees.**
* **75% employer-paid health, dental, and vision** insurance coverage for **dependent(s).**
* **Paid holidays to recharge with loved ones.**
* Access to a confidential **Employee Assistance Program** (EAP).

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* A Bachelor’s degree in healthcare, behavioral health, business administration, or a related field is **required**.
* Five years of progressively responsible healthcare, behavioral health, or substance use disorder treatment leadership experience is **required**.
* Experience supervising managers or department leaders is **required**.
* Experience managing multiple departments or locations, developing operational processes, and leading organizational improvements is preferred.

**Additional Requirements:**

* Successful completion of the pre-employment screening process.

At Heartview Foundation, every team member helps create a safe, recovery-oriented environment. We look for employees who are committed to recovery principles and healthy living, and who can demonstrate that commitment through their professional conduct and personal wellness practices. Because of the unique role we play in clients’ lives, staff must also respect professional boundaries, avoid conflicts of interest, and recognize the power differential that can exist not only between providers and clients but also among staff members. To ensure ethical standards are maintained, employees cannot be current participants in Heartview Foundation’s primary treatment programs. If an offer of employment is made, Human Resources will conduct due diligence to confirm the accuracy of this disclosure.

**Don't miss the chance to join a truly meaningful mission and team making a difference in others' lives every day.** Apply today and embark on a fulfilling career at Heartview Foundation!

**This posting will be open until filled.**

The role requires a dynamic leader who can drive performance improvements, foster a culture of excellence, and support the organization's mission to provide exceptional healthcare services.

**Compensation:** Starting compensation range is $120,000.00-$140,000.00 annually + bonus opportunity. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

* Provide oversight and management of Area Directors and their respective clinic locations (3-8 sites)
* Manage regional budgets including revenue forecasts, expenses, and resource allocation

* Ensure compliance with federal, state, and regulatory requirements across all locations
* Partner with sales and marketing to identify growth opportunities and drive business development
* Analyze operational systems and implement process improvements for efficiency
* Maintain high standards of patient care quality and satisfaction across region
* Resolve complex operational issues and manage stakeholder relationships

* Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

* Multi-site outpatient management experience required
* Occupational health background strongly preferred

* Ability to travel within assigned region up to 50% of the time
* Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
* Interaction with patients, staff, and external stakeholders in potentially challenging situations
* Flexible hours to cover regional operational needs
* Standard office physical demands including computer work and occasional lifting up to 25 pounds
* Occupational health or outpatient facility background strongly preferred
* Medical/clinical certification (MA, LVN, RN) strongly preferred
* Healthcare management certification preferred

The Director of Operations is responsible for the strategic leadership, oversight, and continuous improvement of the Bank's operational functions, systems, and processes. This position provides leadership to the Operations Manager, Treasury Management Sales Officer, and operational staff while ensuring operational excellence, regulatory compliance, risk mitigation, process efficiency, and exceptional employee and customer experiences.

The Director of Operations serves as the Bank's primary business owner for the core processing system and related operational technologies. This role is responsible for maintaining strong relationships with the Bank's core provider and other operational vendors, leading system implementations and enhancements, evaluating operational efficiencies, and ensuring operational resources effectively support the Bank's strategic objectives.

The Director of Operations partners closely with Senior Management, Compliance, Accounting, Retail Banking, Information Technology, and other committees to ensure operational processes, controls, and technologies remain efficient, scalable, and aligned with organizational goals. This position is expected to champion innovation, continuous improvement, and operational excellence throughout the organization.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Directly supervises the Operations Manager and Treasury Management Sales Officer, providing leadership, coaching, performance management, and professional development while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and exceptional service.
* Provides strategic oversight of the Bank's operational functions and develops initiatives that improve efficiency, service quality, scalability, operational effectiveness, and overall customer and employee experience.
* Serves as the primary business owner and relationship manager for the Bank's core processing provider and related operational systems, leading system enhancements, upgrades, conversions, integrations, testing, implementation, training, and user communication.
* Manages relationships with operational vendors and third-party service providers, ensuring service effectiveness and value, regulatory compliance, and identification of technology solutions that improve operational performance.
* Leads operational projects, process improvement initiatives, and cross-functional efforts that streamline workflows, reduce risk, strengthen controls, and enhance service delivery throughout the organization.
* Develops and monitors operational performance metrics and reporting to evaluate departmental effectiveness, identify opportunities for improvement, and support strategic decision-making.
* Ensures operational activities comply with applicable laws, regulations, policies, and internal controls through effective risk management, policy administration, and support of internal and external audits and examinations.
* Serves as the Bank's operational subject matter expert and provides leadership in resolving escalated operational and customer service issues while ensuring responsive support to employees and customers.
* Partners with Senior Management and department leaders to ensure operational processes, controls, and technologies align with organizational objectives and strategic priorities.

Success means dependable service, capable and accountable teams, measurable gains in efficiency, and operations that can support continued growth. This leader learns the business quickly, builds credibility with employees and customers, and consistently turns priorities into results.

* Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations to senior leadership.

* Internal sales, business development, or account management experience, including supporting new-business pursuits, solution design, or account growth.
* Strong leadership, process improvement background, industrial or systems engineering, manufacturing, logistics, or another field requiring disciplined execution and coordination.
* Experience leading managers or multiple operational teams.
* Experience owning technology implementation, process transformation, or other complex cross-functional initiatives.
* MBA or other advanced education relevant to business and operational leadership.

card.description:
**About K12 Coalition**

K12 Coalition provides products and services that help K-12 schools and teachers achieve transformational learning outcomes. We tackle many of today’s toughest education obstacles, including teacher certification, test preparation, professional learning, curriculum, consulting, and strategic planning. K12 Coalition came together when educators with deep experience as teachers, school leaders, and high-level district administrators observed a genuine need for something better. Our divisions include iteach, Passage Preparation, Professional Development Institute, Teaching Channel, Lavinia Group, and Keys to Literacy.

 

**About Lavinia Group**

Lavinia Group is dedicated to driving meaningful academic improvements in K-12 education through instructional coaching, professional learning, high-quality curriculum, strategic planning, and summer school support that enhances educator effectiveness and strengthens student outcomes.

 

With deep expertise in school leadership, curriculum implementation, and instructional best practices, Lavinia Group delivers tailored, research-based solutions to meet the evolving needs of our partners. Guided by a commitment to equity, instructional excellence, and long-term capacity building, we work alongside educators and district leaders through hands-on coaching, immersive training, and collaborative partnerships. Our mission is to help schools achieve transformational learning outcomes that endure beyond our direct support.

 

**Employment Type:**

* Full-Time
* Exempt
* Salaried

 

**Location:** Remote, available from anywhere within the U.S.

 

**The Opportunity**

Lavinia Group, a division of K12 Coalition, is seeking an Operations Director, Curriculum & School Support to build and lead the systems that bring our curriculum and professional learning services to schools. The largest focus of this role is managing the full operational lifecycle of our print curriculum, from demand forecasting and inventory planning to production, fulfillment, and direct customer support. This role also leads operational planning for digital curriculum, professional learning, and consultant staffing outside of our RISE summer learning program.

 

This is an opportunity to help shape how a newly structured operations team works together. Partnering with the Managing Director, Operations and fellow operations leaders, you will help establish clear responsibilities, shared processes, and scalable systems across Lavinia Group while leading execution within your own portfolio. You will turn product and service priorities into practical plans, use technology and AI to improve workflows, and build the operational foundation for new offerings and continued growth.

 

The Operations Director, Curriculum & School Support reports to the Managing Director, Operations and directly manages a Senior Associate, Operations. This role is ideal for an operations leader who enjoys building structure, solving complex delivery challenges, and staying closely involved in day-to-day execution.

 

**What You’ll Do**

Print Curriculum & Fulfillment Operations

* Lead the full print curriculum workflow, including demand forecasting, inventory planning, production schedules, ordering, and fulfillment.
* Partner with Sales and Curriculum teams to translate sales projections, partner needs, and product timelines into purchasing and production plans.
* Manage print vendors, book vendors, and fulfillment partners, including negotiations, performance monitoring, and issue resolution against quality, cost, and delivery expectations.
* Monitor inventory and fulfillment costs, anticipating shortages, excess stock, and delivery risks and adjusting plans as needs change.
* Provide direct customer support for curriculum orders and delivery questions, coordinating timely resolution of fulfillment issues and keeping partners informed.

Operational Systems & Product Implementation

* Build and improve the systems, workflows, and project plans that support curriculum and professional learning development, implementation, and delivery.
* Partner with Curriculum, Product, and Technology teams to define operational requirements for digital curriculum platforms and coordinate improvements that support users and internal teams.
* Establish consistent partner onboarding processes and coordinate operational readiness for product launches, updates, and retirements.
* Use technology, automation, and AI-enabled tools to reduce manual work, improve visibility, and create more reliable, scalable workflows.
* Partner with fellow operations leaders to establish shared practices, clarify team handoffs, and resolve dependencies across Lavinia Group.

Professional Learning & Consultant Staffing

* Lead operational planning for partner-facing professional learning and coaching services, aligning schedules, staffing, resources, and delivery requirements.
* Develop and maintain staffing and capacity plans, partnering with academic and service leaders to forecast facilitator, consultant, and content-development needs.
* Manage consultant staffing and utilization in Hub Planner, maintaining accurate assignments and availability and addressing capacity gaps with relevant leaders.
* Manage workflows for custom professional learning requests, pricing, and approvals in partnership with academic and business leaders.
* Establish operational delivery standards and monitor utilization, delivery days, and partner feedback to identify and implement improvements.

Budget & Performance Management

* Build and manage curriculum, product, and professional learning operating budgets in partnership with the Managing Director, Operations and relevant business leaders.
* Monitor spending, delivery costs, and budget performance, recommending adjustments that align resources with demand and organizational priorities.
* Maintain reporting that gives leaders clear visibility into inventory, fulfillment, staffing capacity, and operational performance.
* Coordinate with finance and sales operations colleagues to ensure accurate information and clear handoffs for invoicing, contracting, and vendor onboarding.

Team Leadership

* Manage and develop the Senior Associate, Operations, setting clear priorities, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
* Provide ongoing coaching and feedback, delegate work effectively, and support professional growth while maintaining accountability for team deliverables.

Other Duties

* Support the team with additional tasks and responsibilities as needed to help meet evolving organizational goals and objectives.

* Bachelor’s degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* At least 5 years of experience in operations, product operations, supply chain, or a related field, including managing complex, cross-functional initiatives.
* Direct experience managing operations for physical products sold to customers, including demand forecasting, inventory planning, production or purchasing coordination, and fulfillment.
* Experience managing vendors and fulfillment partners, including monitoring costs, quality, and delivery performance and resolving customer issues.
* Demonstrated success building scalable operational systems and workflows, including defining operational requirements, partnering across teams to implement improvements, and using AI-enabled tools and automation to reduce manual work.
* Experience managing budgets, analyzing operational data, and developing staffing, capacity, or resource plans.
* Experience managing and developing direct reports, including setting priorities, delegating work, and providing performance feedback.
* Advanced proficiency in Google Workspace, particularly Google Sheets, for forecasting, reporting, data analysis, and operational decision-making, along with experience using project management or workflow tools.
* Strong project management and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate across teams, manage competing priorities, and follow through on commitments.
* Experience in K–12 education, curriculum publishing, or professional learning is preferred but not required.

**How We Work at K12 Coalition**

Our work is grounded in five Core Competencies that guide how we collaborate, support others, and move work forward: Accountability, Adaptability, Collaboration, Customer Service Orientation, and Initiative.

* **Accountability:** Following through on work, owning commitments, and communicating progress or challenges along the way.
* **Adaptability:** Navigating change with flexibility and focus as priorities, information, or needs shift.
* **Collaboration:** Working together across roles and perspectives to achieve shared goals.
* **Customer Service Orientation:** Meeting the needs of internal and external partners with clarity, responsiveness, and follow-through.
* **Initiative:** Taking action without waiting to be asked and looking for ways to improve systems, processes, or experiences.

 

**Compensation Philosophy**

As part of our commitment to maintaining fair and consistent compensation practices, new hires are typically brought into the organization at a salary between the band minimum and midpoint, based on their qualifications, location, internal alignment, and the budgeted amount for the role.

 

**Why Work with Us**

We believe in supporting the whole employee by offering a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet diverse needs. Our full-time employee benefits include flexible time off, paid parental leave, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, and a 401(k) with company matching. We are committed to fostering a work environment that promotes both personal and professional well-being.

 

**Our Typical Selection Process**

Our selection process typically includes an online application, a short phone interview, a hiring manager interview, a candidate exercise, and a final interview.

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

K12 Coalition is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you need assistance or accommodation during the interview process due to a disability, please email us at recruitingteam@k12coalition.com. This information will be treated as confidential and used only for the purpose of determining an appropriate accommodation for the interview process.

 

**Protecting Your Job Search**

K12 Coalition is committed to a transparent and secure recruitment process. Please keep the following in mind as you explore opportunities with us:

* **Official communication:** All recruitment-related communication will come from an @k12coalition.com email address. We do not use messaging platforms for recruiting.
* **Application process:** We do not send unsolicited job offers. All open positions are listed on our official Careers Page, and any offer follows a formal interview process.
* **No upfront payments:** We will never ask candidates to pay fees of any kind during the hiring process, including for training materials, background checks, or equipment.

 

If you receive any communication that does not align with the above, please report it to recruitingteam@k12coalition.com.

**About Us** 
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Visa will accept applications for this role until at least 12-03-2026

**Job Description**

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Data Center IT Operations is a first-line people leader responsible for the safe, reliable, and disciplined execution of Data Center IT Operations across enterprise data center environments. The role oversees teams supporting day-to-day data center operations, mainframe physical infrastructure activities, and storage and tape/media operations while ensuring work is completed to approved scope, service commitments, security requirements, and operational standards.

This position translates Director-level strategy and priorities into daily operating plans, clear accountability, effective staffing, measurable outcomes, and consistent execution. The role provides direct people leadership, operational governance, technical escalation, change and incident oversight, vendor coordination, audit readiness, and continuous improvement across the supported functions.

The Senior Manager is a working people leader. The role is expected to maintain sufficient technical depth to challenge plans, validate readiness, guide escalations, and make risk-based operating decisions, while relying on senior technical contributors and subject-matter experts for detailed engineering authority and platform-specific design decisions.

The Senior Manager collaborates with capacity planning, facilities, DCIM, engineering, finance, and business stakeholders by providing accurate operational data, site constraints, implementation demand, lifecycle information, and risk inputs needed for forecasting and investment decisions.

Proficiency

card.description:
**About the Role:**

The Vice President of Operations in a manufacturing environment is responsible for overseeing and optimizing all operational aspects to ensure efficiency, quality, and profitability. This role requires strategic leadership to align operational goals with the company’s overall vision and market demands. The VP of Operations will drive continuous improvement initiatives, manage cross-functional teams, and implement best practices to enhance production processes and supply chain management. They will also play a critical role in financial planning, resource allocation, and risk management to support sustainable growth. Ultimately, this position ensures that manufacturing operations meet customer expectations while maintaining compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing operations.
* Proven track record of strategic planning and successful execution in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Strong financial acumen with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
* Demonstrated ability to lead large teams and manage cross-functional projects.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA) or relevant advanced degree.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Familiarity with advanced data analytics tools and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
* Previous experience in a senior executive role within the manufacturing industry.
* Certifications related to operations management or leadership development.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute comprehensive operational strategies that support the company’s business objectives and growth plans.
* Lead and mentor senior management and operational teams to foster a culture of high performance, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Oversee production planning, quality control, supply chain logistics, and maintenance to maximize operational efficiency and product quality.
* Collaborate with finance to manage budgets, forecast operational costs, and analyze financial performance to inform decision-making.
* Utilize data analytics to monitor key performance indicators, identify operational risks, and implement corrective actions promptly.
* Drive talent development initiatives to build a skilled and motivated workforce aligned with organizational goals.
* Communicate operational plans, progress, and challenges effectively to the executive leadership team and stakeholders.
* Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental regulations, and industry standards across all manufacturing sites.

**Skills:**

The required skills such as Executive Presence and Leadership are essential for inspiring and guiding diverse teams while representing the operations function at the executive level. Strategic Planning and Execution skills enable the VP to develop actionable roadmaps that align operational activities with long-term business goals. Operational Strategy expertise is applied daily to optimize manufacturing processes, improve supply chain efficiency, and ensure product quality. Communication and Presentation skills are critical for articulating complex operational plans and performance metrics to stakeholders clearly and persuasively. Delegation, Financial Planning and Analysis, Data Analysis, and Talent Development skills are utilized to empower teams, manage resources effectively, make data-driven decisions, and cultivate a high-performing workforce that drives continuous operational excellence.

**Position Summary:**

The Manager, Operations Maintenance (Production) is responsible for overseeing and coordinating production personnel activities and ensuring accurate and timely completion of associated documentation in support ofensuring the operation and maintenance of production (prep, compounding, and filling) machinery and mechanical equipment in compliance with all safety policies, cGMPs, and SOPs. This role works cross-functionally with quality, engineering, manufacturing, technical transfer, and validation. The Manager, Operations Maintenance (Production) will rely on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals, which include organizing hourly employees in the performance of their duties, driving productivity to achieve optimum results, coordinating labor needs in support of minimizing active batch downtime and preventative maintenance schedule attainment. Additionally, the Operations Maintenance Manager (Production) oversees special project for process improvements to the manufacturing process. This position supports the ongoing development, manufacture, and distribution of pharmaceutical products in compliance with local procedures, corporate policies, and the regulatory requirements of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Maintain a sterile environment in the clean room by complying with garbing and behavior requirements that align to established cGMP practices and techniques
* Enforce/follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), safety policies, batch records, current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), including Data Integrity and Good Documentation Practices (GDocP)
* Manage the operations maintenance (production) team to perform responsibilities associated with the troubleshooting/repair/preventative maintenance of GMP utilities and GMP pharmaceutical processing equipment, as well as accurate and timely completion of associated documentation
* Ensure operations maintenance (production) team members adequately support the production operations teams (Prep, Compounding and Fill) with equipment changeovers, set-ups, and start-up activities
* Ensure accurate and complete spare parts inventories are maintained
* Plan and execute operations maintenance (production) shut down/start up activities
* Conduct employee reviews and provide coaching as appropriate; maintain performance and attendance records
* Improve existing processes and/or equipment functionality in order to improve operational efficiency

card.description:
**Sr. Director, KOH Operations**

***Nexpera LLC | Based in Houston, Texas***

Nexpera is an industrial chemistry company serving refining and industrial customers across North America. Our potassium hydroxide business recovers and reprocesses spent KOH from HF alkylation units and other industrial sources, returning specification product to customers who depend on consistent quality and reliable supply. The Sr. Director, KOH Operations leads that business end to end.

**Position Summary**
--------------------

The Sr. Director, KOH Operations holds single-point accountability for the safe, compliant, and profitable operation of five KOH facilities: Houston, Texas; New Orleans, Louisiana; two sites in the Chicago area; and Tamaqua, Pennsylvania. The role owns safety performance, product quality, cost, asset reliability, and the development of the people who run these plants, while driving the growth of the KOH platform alongside commercial partners.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is comfortable in the plant and credible in front of a customer. The successful candidate will spend meaningful time at each site, will set a visible standard for process safety, and will build an operating rhythm that holds five geographically dispersed plants to one common set of expectations.

**Scope of Responsibility**
---------------------------

Five operating facilities across four states, with the leadership team, operating budget, capital program, and customer relationships that support them.

**Facility**

**Location**

Houston

Houston, Texas (also the base for this role)

New Orleans

New Orleans, Louisiana

Chicago area, site 1

Greater Chicago, Illinois

Chicago area, site 2

Greater Chicago, Illinois

Tamaqua

Tamaqua, Pennsylvania

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Safety, Health and Environmental Performance**

Own safety outcomes across all five sites and set the expectation that no production target justifies an unsafe act. Lead process safety management for caustic handling and the associated thermal, pressure, and corrosion hazards, including mechanical integrity, operating windows, management of change, and pre-startup safety review. Ensure each facility maintains its environmental permits and regulatory obligations in good standing, and that incidents, near misses, and high-potential events are investigated to root cause with corrective actions that close on schedule.

### **Operational Execution and Reliability**

Deliver production and on-time delivery commitments across the network, balancing plant capability against customer demand. Establish a consistent operating discipline at all five sites covering shift handover, operating limits, preventive maintenance, and turnaround planning. Drive asset reliability and uptime through disciplined root cause analysis of unplanned outages, and hold the sites to a common standard for maintenance execution rather than letting each plant run its own practice.

### **Product Quality**

Own product quality from feedstock receipt through shipment. Maintain the specification and testing regime that customers rely on, ensure laboratory and analytical capability is sound at each site, and lead the response when a quality deviation reaches a customer. Build the trend data and process controls that prevent repeat excursions rather than catching them at final test.

### **Growth**

Partner with commercial leadership to grow volume and margin in the KOH platform. Identify and unlock latent capacity within the existing asset base, evaluate debottlenecking and expansion opportunities, and provide the operating input that underpins new customer agreements and onsite service offerings. Support evaluation of new facility locations and acquisition opportunities, including the operational due diligence and integration planning that follow.

### **EBITDA Growth and Cost Management**

Build and own the operating and capital budgets for the KOH network, and deliver against them. Manage variable cost per ton, labor, maintenance spend, logistics, and third-party services with an understanding of what drives each. Prepare and defend capital authorization requests, and hold projects to their approved scope, schedule, and cost once funded.

### **People and Organizational Development**

Lead, coach, and develop the site leadership teams, and build the bench that supplies the next generation of plant managers. Set clear performance expectations, conduct meaningful reviews, and address performance gaps directly. Own staffing plans, succession, and the technical training that keeps operators and maintenance crews competent in a caustic-handling environment, and work to make Nexpera a place skilled people choose to stay.

### **Continuous Improvement**

Establish a common set of operating metrics across the five sites and use them to find and close performance gaps. Transfer best practice between plants deliberately rather than by accident, so that a fix proven in Tamaqua reaches Houston and Chicago. Sponsor structured improvement work on yield, energy, cycle time, and labor productivity, and build the expectation at every level that this year's performance is the baseline, not the target.

**Qualifications**
------------------

### **Required**

Bachelor's degree in chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Twelve or more years in chemical, refining, or process manufacturing operations, including at least five years leading a plant or a multi-site operation.

Demonstrated ownership of safety and process safety performance in a hazardous chemical environment, with working command of PSM elements and OSHA and EPA regulatory obligations.

Full profit and loss or operating budget accountability, including capital planning and project justification.

A record of developing people and building leadership teams, not simply managing them.

Willingness to travel regularly to the four sites outside Houston, estimated at 30 to 40 percent.

### **Preferred**

Direct experience with caustic, potassium hydroxide, or spent-chemical recovery and regeneration processes.

Experience serving refining customers or operating within a customer's fence line.

Multi-site leadership across geographically separated plants.

Formal continuous improvement training, such as Lean or Six Sigma, applied in a process environment.

Advanced degree in engineering or business.

Merger and acquisition integration or greenfield facility startup experience.

**Working Conditions**
----------------------

Based in the Houston office with regular travel to New Orleans, the two Chicago-area sites, and Tamaqua. Time in operating plants requires the use of personal protective equipment and the ability to work around caustic chemicals, elevated temperatures, and rotating equipment. The role carries an on-call expectation for significant operational and safety events across the network.

**Organizational Relationships**
--------------------------------

Close working partnerships are expected with commercial leadership on customer commitments and growth, with EHS on safety and regulatory standards, with supply chain and logistics on feedstock and product movement, with engineering and capital projects on asset investment, and with finance and human resources on budget and staffing.

*Nexpera is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to any characteristic protected by law.*

card.title: Director of Operations
card.description:
Advanced Mission Partners, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Science Systems and Applications, Inc (SSAI) seeks a Director of Operations to provide strategic and operational leadership across our aerospace component manufacturing, electronics manufacturing, and engineering services operations. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing daily operations, optimizing manufacturing performance, managing resources, and ensuring the successful delivery of high-quality products and engineering services. This position will play a critical role in driving operational excellence, improving profitability, strengthening customer relationships, and supporting the company's continued growth. 
The ideal candidate will have a strong background in aerospace and defense manufacturing, demonstrated leadership experience, and a proven ability to manage complex manufacturing operations while meeting demanding quality, cost, and delivery requirements.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree (BS) in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, Project Management, Operations Management, or a related technical discipline.
* 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in program management, project management, manufacturing operations, or engineering.
* At least 5 years of experience managing complex technical or manufacturing programs, preferably within the aerospace, defense, or electronics manufacturing industries.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations, managing budgets, and improving operational performance.
* Experience working with aerospace and defense customers, including government agencies, prime contractors, and commercial aerospace organizations.
* Working knowledge of manufacturing processes, engineering development, quality assurance, and supply chain management.
* Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and implementing operational improvement initiatives.
* Strong financial, analytical, leadership, and problem-solving skills.

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
* Experience in aerospace component manufacturing, electronics manufacturing services (EMS), or precision manufacturing.
* Familiarity with printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), electronic systems integration, and aerospace manufacturing processes.
* Knowledge of AS9100, ISO 9001, IPC standards, and applicable aerospace quality requirements.
* Experience with government contracts, including FAR, DFARS, ITAR, and EAR requirements.
* Familiarity with Earned Value Management (EVM), program financial forecasting, and cost control methodologies.
* Experience using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and project management software, such as Microsoft Project or equivalent tools.
* Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI), production transitions, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Demonstrated experience with manufacturing automation, process optimization, and production scalability.

**EOE, including disability/vets**

***Physical Requirements:*** *While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, and use hands to touch, handle or feel objects, tools or controls. The employee frequently is required to talk and hear and occasionally required to reach with hands and arms and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.*
